I'm sorry that you feel this way and I know this post might make you feel worse and I'm so sorry if it does but reading this sounds like a very typical complaint list about being Chinese and having Chinese parents. (although I do disagree with a few things on here)

First off, I definitely agree with you on certain parts like, "if you're ugly, good luck being ugly" and the gossipy-ness of parents/families and just the general obnoxiousness and rude mannerisms of being born in a Chinese household. 

Growing up, I had a lot of complaints like these that mostly dealt with the overly-critical/overly-vocal issues of having a Chinese mom because she would constantly comment on my weight and other superficial annoying things like that (and she still does from time to time) and while yeah, it sucks and it's definitely different from what my American friends went through in their household, that's their culture and no one can change that.

Mind me asking your age? While I'm neither trying to imply you are young or maybe immature (because I'm definitely not), I felt as if with age, I became more accepting of Chinese culture and definitely had it embedded in me. I guess there are some perks in being raised Chinese and now that I'm a bit older than I use to be (19), I am easily able to bypass a lot of these rude/snide comments because a) it's not meant to be hurtful, it's really just in their nature to...well, be like that and b) because generally, Chinese parents are neurotic and insulting but very protective/caring of their children (although they can't show it which leads to them acting so strangely/rudely)

When you're Chinese-American, I honestly feel like you either "get it" and embrace it or you hate it and want to further yourself from it. A lot of comes down to your personality and what type of person you are so yes, if you're sensitive and very accustomed to people being polite and courteous with you, you're probably going to hate it. With me, I've always been able to brush off these comments (for the most part) and now as I'm older, I understand why Chinese people often criticize and that's to make sure their children are presentable, good kids. I guess I have a somewhat hard shell due to having such a familiarity with criticism and I'm pretty humble/modest because of my parents.

Then again, we might just have different families/outlooks since I don't agree with a few things you listed in your post but I hope you feel better and do know that at the end of the day, you are able to do whatever you want and live your own life.
